variant: Character LoRA trained on real photographs. The output is a reusable identity asset, not a film: any later project loads it with a trigger token instead of carrying a master into every shot.
title: Ivy — character LoRA
status: training 2026-09-26 — 22 image/caption pairs, 2000 steps, checkpoints every 400
source: real photographs of Ivy, curated into raw/ (git-ignored)
notes: Ivy is family, an adult; consent settled, same standing as Kyle and Lindsey. Real photos are the better dataset: B0 proved klein will not synthesize back views or true camera-height variation from a frontal master, because the reference image overrides the prompt. Photographs have those angles already — except that this particular set does not: all 22 frames are frontal or three-quarter. raw/ is git-ignored because consent to train on a face is not consent to publish the source photographs to a public repo.

dataset.subject: girl
dataset.caption_rule: Isolation Rule — caption only what varies (framing, angle, expression, clothing, background, light). Face, hair and permanent features are omitted so they bind to the trigger token. This is the inverse of how our shot prompts are written.
dataset.captioning: by hand, one photo at a time, after looking at it — a generated caption that names a permanent feature silently un-binds that feature from the trigger
dataset.status: built 2026-09-26, captions hand-written after viewing each frame
dataset.composition: 16 supplied photographs + 6 reframes cropped from their own 2048 px originals
dataset.class_word: woman — the trigger is always followed by a class word
dataset.known_gap: no profile and no back-of-head frames; the supplied set contains none

training.measured_on_nightelf: 0.22 it/s, 2 h 31 m for 2000 steps, 402 MB per checkpoint
training.evaluate: scripts/lora_eval.sh with a no-LoRA control column; the 2000-step checkpoint won on the night elf with no sign of overfitting
